limitations: Claude Code does not report user interrupts directly. runmarq infers them and marks those runs cancelled, never finished.
Plan progress is available only when Claude keeps a task list or to-do list.
Model metadata is reported at session start, not for every prompt.
Requires Codex 0.130 or later, and the runmarq hooks must be trusted once with /hooks inside Codex.
Codex 0.130 has no tool-failure, interrupt or session-end hooks. Failed shell commands are detected from exit codes when Codex reports them.
Start Codex with `runmarq run -- codex` to have runs closed when the process exits.
Already-running Codex IDE sessions that were started without hooks cannot be observed.
mechanism: Codex lifecycle hooks (hooks.json) and the runmarq run wrapper

limitations: Tool start and approval events are not collected: Cursor's pre-execution hooks can block or auto-approve actions, so runmarq does not register them.
Cursor does not document which shell runs hooks on Windows. Verify the integration after setup.
Project hooks run only in trusted workspaces. Integrated-terminal commands you run yourself are not agent activity and are not tracked.
Cursor does not write a session transcript runmarq can read, so its runs have no token counts.
